expectations.text: The spec starts from the decisions or management questions the Commercial Director must answer, before listing KPIs.
expectations.evidence: weekly_commercial_dashboard_spec.md section 2 'Decisions supported' lists five decisions with the action each drives (where to push this week; fix execution vs accept market slowdown and reforecast; hold back shipments to avoid loading the trade; re-allocate or stop promotions; where the field force goes next week). Section 1 also has a 'one-minute test'. This comes before the KPI dictionary (section 4).

expectations.text: Each headline KPI has a definition, formula or source field, refresh/latency, a target or threshold (or an explicit 'to be confirmed'), and polarity (which direction is good).
expectations.evidence: Every headline KPI (1-7) has a fixed block: Question, Formula, Source/grain, Refresh/latency, Target, Polarity ('Higher is better' / 'Lower is better (up to the cap)'), Status rule, Owner, Caveats. Missing items are explicit [TBD: ..., owner: ...] (e.g. net sales target source/grain, purchase-event source for coverage, OOS 'None formal'). Driver metrics table also carries Source, Target/band and Polarity columns.

expectations.text: It addresses the data latency/grain mismatches and quality caveats in the source (IQVIA sell-out monthly with ~4-week lag versus a weekly dashboard; retail-audit sample skew; CRM outlet duplicates) and says how the dashboard shows them.
expectations.evidence: Top 'Read this first' box and section 4: sell-in/CRM daily vs sell-out '~4 weeks after month end -> latest data is two months old', Finance close+6 WD, OOS biweekly; weekly and monthly KPIs visually separated on Page 1 with their own as-of dates; 'Never disaggregate monthly data to weeks'; filter-compatibility matrix labels visuals that ignore the week slicer. OOS: 'Panel OOS (400-store audit)', 'Large chains / Southeast over-represented', suppress small n, no extrapolation. Duplicates: coverage on golden outlet ID, 'Provisional: outlet master x% deduplicated' badge, 0.82 effect worked and labeled as an assumption to confirm.

expectations.text: It defines a visual hierarchy/layout (what sits at the top vs drill-down) and chart choices justified by the question each answers.
expectations.evidence: Section 3 gives a page table plus a Page 1 wireframe with zones (weekly vs monthly KPI strip, Needs-attention list, gap-to-target variance bars, driver bullet graphs), KPI card anatomy, drill path to pages 2-5 and Customer/SKU drill-through. Each KPI carries an explicit 'Question' it answers, chart rules are stated ('No gauges, donuts or maps. A map is not needed: region is compared as sorted bars'), and pages are tied to the numbered decisions.

expectations.text: RAG/status colors are defined by business thresholds and metric polarity, not merely by up/down movement.
expectations.evidence: Status rules are thresholds against targets with explicit polarity per KPI (Higher/Lower is better), status is icon + word + color with colors by favorable/unfavorable rather than up/down, 'no target -> No target in grey', plus a 'watermelon' rule so a total cannot be green when a material component is red. Acceptance test 3 checks each rule at, above and below every threshold per polarity.

expectations.text: It specifies interactions (filters, drill-downs) and non-happy-path states (stale data, missing data, loading/empty/error) or explicitly scopes them out.
expectations.evidence: Section 8 Interactions (synced slicers, reset, drill path with back buttons, drill-through, tooltips, partial period styling) and a Section 9 States table covering Stale, Partial, No target, Empty ('Never a 0 that reads as real'), Low sample and Error (source name + last good as-of). Loading is not mentioned explicitly, but stale/missing/empty/error are specified with behavior and acceptance test 9 forces each state.

expectations.text: The top level is limited to a focused set of headline KPIs (roughly 9 or fewer) rather than every available metric.
expectations.evidence: Seven headline KPI cards on Page 1 (net sales MTD, month landing, coverage, panel OOS, sell-out growth, trade spend %, contribution margin); call-plan compliance, sell-in/sell-out ratio, price index and gross-to-net are demoted to driver metrics without a headline card.

expectations.text: It does not invent targets absent from the data description; the OOS threshold is labeled informal (5%) or to-be-confirmed.
expectations.evidence: OOS: 'None formal. The team uses 5% informally. Show Reference 5% (informal, not approved) as a grey reference line. No status color until a target is approved' - no RAG on OOS at all. Other targets are either from the data (net sales target, 75% coverage, 8.5% cap) or [TBD]. The only invented bands (net sales 98-100%, trade spend 8.0-8.5%, WD 5 suppression) are explicitly marked '(proposed)' with 'proposed, to be confirmed' shown in tooltips and page 6; all others are [TBD]. Final message repeats this. Minor: numbers_check lists some design parameters as untraced, but they are structural, not targets.

strengths: Every headline KPI follows the same contract (Question, Formula, Source/grain, Refresh/latency, Target, Polarity, Status rule, Owner, Caveats), with unknowns explicitly [TBD: ..., owner: ...] rather than guessed; targets are only the given ones (net sales, 75%, 8.5% cap), the 5% OOS is a grey informal reference with no status color, and the few suggested bands are labeled 'proposed'.

Excellent integrity framing: a 'Read this first' box leads with the two risks that change the answer (duplicate-inflated denominator, with the 0.82 effect shown as an assumption; weekly vs monthly source mixing), plus a filter-compatibility matrix showing which slicers each source ignores.

Decision-first structure (five decisions each tied to an action), seven headline KPIs max, a Needs-attention exceptions engine with sentence templates and R$ at stake, and a no-watermelon status rule.

Complete build contract beyond KPIs: states table (stale/partial/no target/empty/low sample/error), interactions, RLS, data model and mapping tables as critical path, 10 acceptance tests, 11 owner-assigned open questions with blocking status.
defects: Long (about 28 KB) with many TBDs and extra machinery (watermelon materiality threshold, RLS test users, price/volume/mix bridge), so the BI team has to resolve a lot before building; some of it is more than a first version needs.
Loading state is not specified, and with so many TBD bands most statuses will show 'no target' until owners respond.
Costlier process (13 turns, skill and script runs) for the same single deliverable; final chat message is long, though it adds the key risks.
